subject: general
question: The division of subjects between the Union and the States is laid out in which Schedule of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Schedule VII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **division of subjects** between the Union and the States is outlined in **Schedule VII** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Schedule VII contains three lists—**Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**—that distribute legislative powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects such as defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy, over which only the Parliament has exclusive legislative power.
 
• The **State List** includes subjects such as police, public health, and agriculture, over which only the State Legislatures can legislate.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects such as education, marriage, and bankruptcy, over which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate, but in case of a conflict, the law enacted by Parliament prevails.
 
• The division of powers is based on the principle of **federalism**, allowing a clear demarcation of responsibilities and avoiding overlap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Schedule IX:**

 
 
• This schedule was introduced by the **First Amendment** to the Constitution in 1951.
 
• It includes laws that are shielded from judicial review under Article 31B, ensuring their immunity from challenges based on fundamental rights violations.
 
• This schedule was primarily created to protect land reform and agrarian laws from being struck down by courts.
 
• However, in the **2007 I.R. Coelho vs. State of Tamil Nadu case**, the Supreme Court ruled that laws under Schedule IX are not completely immune and can be reviewed if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Schedule V:**
 
 
• This schedule deals with the administration and control of **Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes** in states other than those in the North-Eastern region.
 
• It empowers the President to declare certain areas as Scheduled Areas and provides for the establishment of Tribal Advisory Councils.
 
• Provisions under this schedule aim to protect the rights and culture of Scheduled Tribes and ensure their socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Schedule X:**
 
 
• This schedule was added by the **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**, and is also known as the **Anti-Defection Law**.
 
• It lays down provisions for the disqualification of Members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection.
 
• Defection occurs when elected members voluntarily give up their party membership or vote against their party's direction in the legislature.
 
• The presiding officer of the legislature is the authority to decide on disqualification under this schedule, although this decision is subject to judicial review.
